key_insight: Instead of relying on repeated sampling of near-duplicate LLM answers, the paper learns a small concept-level search policy that proposes diverse reasoning ideas to guide downstream solution generation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to spend test-time compute more effectively for hard reasoning tasks by training a lightweight policy model that can improve and transfer search quality for larger frozen LLMs.
method: Sample problem-specific concepts, hints, or strategies first, then condition answer generation on them.
Generate many diverse concepts in a single trajectory to increase semantic exploration beyond local decoding noise.
Train a small concept generator with reinforcement learning so its concepts maximize the success of a frozen answer generator.
evidence_signal: On hard mathematical reasoning problems, the trained concept generator improves pass@k over naive repeated sampling at the same answer budget and transfers to unseen answer models, including a different model family.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on a separately trained concept policy and the quality of the downstream answer generator, so training cost, transfer reliability, and domain specificity need careful validation.
paper_title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
